title: Kung Pao Chicken
subtitle: Sichuan stir-fried chicken with chillies and peanuts
excerpt: The great Sichuan stir-fry: tender cubes of chicken cooked with dried chillies and Sichuan pepper until numbing and hot, finished with crunchy peanuts in a glossy, savoury sauce that balances sweet, sour, and fiercely spiced.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kung Pao chicken (宫保鸡丁) is named after Ding Baozhen, a Qing Dynasty official who served as governor of Sichuan province and was given the title Gong Bao (Palace Guardian). His love of the dish led to it being named after his title. The dish combines chicken with dried chillies, Sichuan peppercorns, and peanuts in a sauce that exemplifies the mala (numbing-hot) flavour profile central to Sichuan cooking. The Sichuan peppercorns provide ma (numbing) while the dried chillies provide la (spicy heat). Velveting the chicken — coating it in cornflour and marinating briefly before cooking — is the technique that gives the chicken its tender, silky texture.

content.text: The wok must be smoking before the chicken goes in; on a domestic hob, work in a very small batch. Do not move the chicken immediately; let it sit for 30 seconds to develop colour before tossing. Have the sauce ready to pour in the moment the chicken is cooked; the dish moves very fast.

items.preparation: boneless, skinless; cut into 2 cm cubes
dried whole chillies; seeds shaken out
use Sichuan peppercorns if available; lightly crushed

content.text: Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar in a small bowl for the sauce. In a separate bowl, toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and a pinch of cornflour. Set aside for 10 minutes.

Heat the oil in a wok until smoking. Add the dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns (or coriander seeds). Stir-fry for 20 seconds until the oil is fragrant and the chillies darken slightly. Add the chicken in a single layer. Cook without moving for 30 seconds, then stir-fry for 2 minutes until cooked through.
Add the garlic, ginger, and spring onion. Stir-fry for 30 seconds. Pour in the sauce. Toss to coat. Add the peanuts and toss briefly. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
